title: Simulate Automatic Batching Across Async Boundaries
subtopicTitle: Automatic Batching in React 18 vs flushSync
concept: React 18 Universal Batching across Promises & Timeouts
problemStatement: Implement `simulateAsyncBatching(actionFns, onRender)` that executes async callbacks (like `fetch.then`) and verifies that multiple dispatches inside the async handler are batched together.
interviewTrap: In React 17, `setTimeout(() => { setCount(1); setFlag(true); })` fired 2 renders. In React 18, it fires 1 render.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: In React 17, state updates inside `setTimeout` or `Promise.then` were NOT batched, triggering multiple re-renders. React 18 automatically batches ALL state updates regardless of origin. `flushSync(() => { ... })` opts out of batching, forcing an immediate synchronous DOM flush.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How did React 18's Automatic Batching change update behavior across async boundaries?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In React 17 and earlier, batching ONLY worked inside synthetic React event handlers. Updates inside `setTimeout`, `Promise.then()`, or native `fetch` callbacks were NOT batched, triggering multiple independent re-renders. In React 18, 'Automatic Batching' batches ALL updates universally, regardless of whether they occur inside promises, timeouts, or native event listeners.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Crucial difference between React 17 and React 18.

realWorldUseCases.scenario: Asynchronous Fetch Callback Updates in React 18
realWorldUseCases.description: Updating data, loading, and error states inside a `fetch().then()` block produces exactly 1 render in React 18 vs 3 renders in React 17.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: fetch().then(() => { setData(res); setLoading(false); setError(null); }); // 1 render in React 18!

howToExplain.opening: React 18 introduced Automatic Batching, extending state batching across all asynchronous boundaries including promises, timeouts, and native events.
keyPoints: React 17 only batched inside synthetic React event handlers.
React 18 batches universally across microtasks and macrotasks.
Reduces re-renders significantly in data-fetching components.
Opt out via flushSync when immediate DOM updates are required.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Automatic batching is one of React 18's greatest out-of-the-box performance upgrades, requiring zero code changes.
analogies: A bus that waits for all passengers from the delayed train (async promise) to board before departing, instead of driving off with one person at a time.

commonMistakes.mistake: Thinking setTimeout is not batched in React 18.
commonMistakes.why: In React 18, updates inside setTimeout ARE batched by default.
commonMistakes.correct: Clarify that all asynchronous updates are batched in React 18.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React 18 schedule automatic batch flushes internally?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Updates are pushed onto the fiber lane queue and scheduled via a microtask (`ensureRootIsScheduled`), collapsing all updates that occur in the same tick.
